title: You think you’re having a bad day?
excerpt: We often have one of those days where nothing really goes your way. Three ways to put a bad day back in perspective.
content:
We often have one of those days where nothing really goes your way.

Your routine is interrupted, your plans are all squashed, you may have to go through emotional or financial distress, you might have to deal with a health issue or have to take care of a family member, you might have a personal setback — a job loss, a breakup, a fight with a friend or loved one, even loss of property or injury due to an act of god or an act of malice. And of course you never saw it coming.

In the moment, either you act — you do what needs to be done to resolve the bad situation, or you ask for help from someone else, if there is someone to ask.

But after the day has passed, you might end up feeling dejected or frustrated about why it happened to you, why you are unlucky, why God is against you, why you’re having such a bad freaking day.

Some of us have to go through a series of these bad days, or months, or years. And when these “bad” days keep piling up over time, you probably start losing hope, start losing the spark of curiosity or fantasy that you used to have, and become bitter and jaded from all the hits you’ve been taking.

The vicious cycle

I know how this feels since I am going through the same thing in my current phase of life. It’s hard. It’s paralyzing and it creates a vicious cycle: since things aren’t going your way, you feel down and dejected, and since you feel down and dejected, you’re unable to do what needs to be done to make things go your way.

Some things are in your control, and some are not

Now this is where we need to be careful because we enter the territory of the dichotomy of control, as the Stoics put it — that some things in life are in our control and some things are not. Captain obvious here, but I’m not sure we’re as good as we think at telling which situation is which. I guess that is the primary task of life, better put in words by Epictetus:

*The chief task in life is simply this: to identify and separate matters so that I can say clearly to myself which are externals not under my control, and which have to do with the choices I actually control. Where then do I look for good and evil? Not to uncontrollable externals, but within myself to the choices that are my own.

Epictetus, Discourses 2.5.4–5

The point of this essay is to put these “bad days” or “bad situation” in perspective along three dimensions — 1) the dichotomy of control — or what part of the bad situation we can truly impact, 2) perspective — is it truly as bad as you think relative to what other people are going through, and 3) luck / chance / providence — can it be worse? You bet it can be.

Is it truly as bad as you think?

This second part — perspective — is a frame of reference to help us calibrate whether a situation is really as bad as it feels, or whether our minds are making it worse than it actually is. Often, the folks who are stuck in this rut — I assume — are most likely to be either introverted, or to have gone through enough trauma to have turned them more inward-looking than outward-looking. We think we’re the center of the universe, and rightly so — we are the ones experiencing it in the first person, and all of this is happening to us in real-time, all the reality and all the thoughts and emotions — the human experience.

But we often forget, especially during such times of distress, that we live in a world with 8 billion other humans, and infinite species of plants, animals and other life. We’re not alone. Of course, I’m not asking you to compare your life to that of your pet (because you will get depressed fast) or to that of a tree, but we should sometimes think about everyone who is far far far more unlucky than we are.

To begin with, just the fact that you are able to read my blog probably puts you above half the population in the world — people who live in abject poverty, lack internet access, cannot read, or are surviving war, famine, and natural disasters. And then, if you happen to be someone like me living in a city like Seattle, earning decent money, having a comfortable apartment and a car, and having at least a small circle of friends, then you’re easily in the top 1% of the entire planet. I can keep slicing these segments finer and finer, but I think you get the point. Thanks to social media’s ascent in the mid-2010s, as a society we’re now in the habit of constant comparison — and only against those who appear better off or happier than we are. It’s all fake, folks.

Could it be worse? Yes

And finally, the third dimension: the nature of the universe, and the governing laws of what makes everything tick — randomness, chance, luck, providence — whatever you want to call it. We can never see the whole picture, even in hindsight. There are too many angles, too many effects on our lives from unforeseen and indirect sources — the degree of randomness that determines the course of our lives, especially the most significant events, is extremely high. Ultimately, this boils down to asking yourself a single question every time you feel down in the dumps:

Could it be worse? — Yes. You bet. It can be infinitely worse. Every single time, and in every single situation.

Happened to me recently. All my personal plans got disrupted — I had to do international travel to help a family member in need of medical attention. During travel, I got stranded at an airport because the country’s ATC went down. After reaching the destination, another family member fell critically ill and needed intensive care. Two days later, I came down with a fever and congestion — but I still had to assist my parent with those hospital visits, twice a day, come back home, and work at night. And I had to pick up driving again in a place I hadn’t driven in 12 years, with no other option. To some, this may be nothing, and I commend you for being that way. For me, it was a lot and I was mopey and dejected, projecting all this onto the future, impacting my present. But again, if I ask myself, could it have been worse? Hell, freaking YES. At every single point, all of this could have been a million times worse, and just the fact that I’m able to write about all this in peace right now at my place, sitting in my bed, and publishing on a blog, means that all of this was nothing compared to what could have been.

This is where expectation vs. reality comes in: how bad we think our experiences are versus what they objectively are.

To summarize: the goal, especially mine, is to build the mental faculties to stay poised enough to hold these three things in mind when our peace gets disrupted — to put things in the right perspective.

  • What is in your control vs not? — Act on what you can control
  • Is it truly as bad as you think? — Don’t compare to those above you; there are a lot of people who’d kill to be in your situation
  • Could it be worse? — Yes. Every single time. And be grateful that it wasn’t.

So what actually works?

How can you do this? I won’t recommend any self-help books. I’ve read all of them, watched all the videos, and listened to all the podcasts. Two simple practices are all you need: 1) mindfulness — cut away distractions as much as possible, slow down, breathe, and focus on whatever you need to do, and 2) action — keep working, keep moving, keep doing whatever you need to do, not as a nervous wreck, but lightly, sincerely and with low expectations.

Hope you found this useful. I’d love to hear stories if any of this resonated with you. Thanks for stopping by my old-school blog.

title: Pop Culture Philosophy Series #1: Linkin Park
excerpt: [Long post alert, but it’s worth it] If you’ve been a reader of my blog since I started it in 2008 (unlikely), you’ll have picked up that my proclivity towards retaining and finding meaning pop culture is second to none. content:
[Long post alert, but it’s worth it]

If you’ve been a reader of my blog since I started it in 2008 (unlikely), you’ll have picked up that my proclivity towards retaining and finding meaning pop culture is second to none. I guess I must thank my parents to give me access to all that, and secondly to also help build the right type of curiosity that is able to extract deep meaning from the banality of pop culture, movies, music, anime etc.

There are several things that have inspired me over my life and the most important one has been the music of early 2000s rock band Linkin Park. Read about their history and what drove their fame on Wikipedia so I don’t have to repeat the facts.

What I want to dive into are specific songs and the meaning and philosophy behind them. Overall, Linkin Park’s music was extremely human, not preachy, not dreamy, but as real as it could be. The songs meet you in the moment of where you are, and majority of the themes are around mental health – depression, trauma, anger, sadness – all the emotions that truly define humans. This is also why their music has always appealed to me, and appeals to me even more today at 37 than it did when I was 17. As a teenager, I appreciated Chester’s screaming, the heavy guitar and angry music, but now as a fully grown man, I appreciate the meaning behind every song. And I love the new lead Emily Armstrong as well!

I’m gonna go through quite a few songs that provide that depth of human experience to the listener. These are also songs I remember by heart, and they’re capable of moistening the tear glands of this brute with quite some ease.

Read on and drop in a comment in case any of these songs appealed to you, and especially if they appealed differently to you.

Table of Contents

  1. Inner pain
    1. Crawling
    2. Papercut
    3. Heavy
  2. Forced expectations and anger
    1. Numb
    2. A Place for My Head
    3. One Step Closer
  3. Loss, futility, remembrance
    1. In the End
    2. With You
    3. My December
    4. One More Light
  4. Wanting to change, and to be someone else
    1. Breaking the Habit
    2. Somewhere I Belong
    3. Iridescent
    4. Waiting for the End

Inner pain

Crawling, Papercut and Heavy – these ones describe different forms of internal stress, whether it’s about self-judgement, past trauma, inner criticism, and just not having that feeling of control that we all crave.

Crawling

This lack of self-control, I fear is never-ending
…
Discomfort, endlessly has pulled itself upon me
…
Against my will, I stand beside my own reflection
…
These wounds, they will not heal
Fear is how I fall
Confusing, confusing what is real

One of the most recognizable openings to any song (LP has a ton of those), but this song hits you hard if you’ve ever had anything from your past that you know is always there, always affecting you, but you also have no way to do anything about it. That’s the “lack of self-control”, that’s the “against my will”, that’s the “confusing what is real” – these thoughts and feelings crawling under your skin whether you like it or not.

Crawling Lyrics | Krwling Reanimation (best version of the song)

Papercut

Like a face that I hold inside
A face that awakes when I close my eyes
A face that watches every time I lie
A face that laughs every time I fall
(And watches everything)
…
I know I’ve got a face in me
Points out all my mistakes to me
You’ve got a face on the inside too
Your paranoia’s probably worse

This song is close to my heart because it was the song that saved me from hazing / ragging in my freshman / first year of undergrad back in 2006. I didn’t attend a great school and it was in a not so prestigious location, with a ton of brash & rowdy seniors who took a lot of enjoyment in humiliating a freshman. They’d give out unrealistic challenges and if you’re not able to do it, then you gotta do questionable stuff for them. Mine was to sing Papercut, and of course I did. Yes, I can rap. It blew their minds, saved my ass, made me some new friends, and then they asked me to haze the other freshmen. I’ll stop the story right here.

This song though is about that self-criticism hiding beneath your skin, that voice that always second guesses you, the feelings of insecurity, the fear of failure or being paranoid about failure, watching everything you say. You know if you know it. It’s a hard hitting song.

Papercut Lyrics

Heavy

I don’t like my mind right now
Stacking up problems that are so unnecessary
Wish that I could slow things down
I wanna let go but there’s comfort in the panic
And I drive myself crazy
Thinking everything’s about me
…
I keep dragging around what’s bringing me down
If I just let go, I’d be set free

The opening of this song hits you instantly! “I don’t like my mind right now” .. yeah you know when the mind is in a weird place. On one hand, the song takes you through the pain this person is feeling and again that lack of self-control about being able to do anything about it. But on the other hand, it kinda shows you exceptional self-awareness that you’re able to see what’s happening in your mind, and if you just let go of whatever you’re dragging around, you’ll be set free. It’s a sad but also a hopeful song at the same time.

Forced expectations and anger

Numb, A Place for my Head and One Step Closer – some of the angrier songs by LP especially the latter two. It’s understandable, because these are about the expectations put upon you that you’re not able to fulfill, and it leads to overwhelm, pain and anger.

Numb

I’m tired of being what you want me to be
Feeling so faithless, lost under the surface
I don’t know what you’re expecting of me
Put under the pressure of walking in your shoes
…
I’m becoming this, all I want to do
Is be more like me and be less like you
…
And I know
I may end up failing too
But I know
You were just like me with someone disappointed in you

Between “In the end” and “Numb”, these are probably the MJ and LeBron of LP’s song portfolio. Numb again opens with an absolute hard-hitting line “I’m tired of being what you want me to be”, and you’re instantly drawn into the song, connected through that shared feeling of just not being able to be whoever you’re supposed to be. This is another remarkably self-aware song, not just one about frustration, but you can see the shift when you hear “I want to be more like me, and be less like you”, and especially the ending “But I know, you were just like me with someone disappointed in you”. LP shows the pain and anger, but also shows what the person really wants (to be more like themselves), and also compassion for this other person who might also be a victim of this endless cycle of failing to meet expectations.

Numb Lyrics

A Place for My Head

I watch how the moon sits in the sky in the dark night
Shining with the light from the sun
And the sun doesn’t give light to the moon assuming
The moon’s gonna owe it one
…
You try to take the best of me, go away
You try to take the best of me, go away
(angry Chester screams)

This song is actually quite similar to Numb, but much much much angrier. This is also my fav song to rap along with – thanks to the GOAT Mike Shinoda. Another banger of an opener with the Sun & Moon metaphor of how the Sun is not giving the light to moon assuming it’s doing it a favor for something back in return. But for us humans, with our complex relationships with our loved ones, parents etc. this conditional love is far too common. And when the burden of expectations becomes too great, you will eventually want the other person to “go away”.

LP did a live concert in Texas (Dallas) in the early 2000s. It’s probably the greatest rock concert of all time, but I’d especially recommend watching A Place for My Head from that. You just need to hear Chester to feel what the song is trying to communicate.

A Place for My Head Lyrics

One Step Closer

I cannot take this anymore
Saying everything I’ve said before
…
Everything you say to me
Takes me one step closer to the edge
And I’m about to break
…
Shut up when I’m talking to you
Shut up, shut up, shut up

The angriest one of them all. One Step Closer warns you from the opening line “I cannot take this anymore”, with anger and with fire, that if you come closer then someone will just get burned. It’s when you’ve either tried explaining yourself and it doesn’t work, or if you keep hearing words that don’t get through to you, or don’t understand. This song takes you to the point of breaking, and if you know about Chester’s background, he was probably there every time he was singing this song.

One Step Closer Lyrics

Loss, futility, remembrance

In The End, With You, My December, One More Light – sadness, loss, futility, remembrance. Also my absolute favorite sing-along tracks.

In the End

One thing, I don’t know why
It doesn’t even matter how hard you try
…
I kept everything inside
And even though I tried, it all fell apart
What it meant to me will eventually be
A memory of a time when I tried so hard
…
I tried so hard and got so far
But in the end, it doesn’t even matter

Probably the greatest and most recognizable LP song ever. Another super hard-hitter for someone like me. It hits especially hard for ambitious people who think that if you put in the effort, you’re entitled to the results. Life doesn’t work that way, and there are no guarantees. You keep trying and trying to force the outcomes you want, you try and you fail, and then you remember those times. The reanimation version’s lyrics then point out the reflective part of the song:

But in the end, no matter what I pretend
The journey is more important than the end or the start

In the end lyrics

With You

I woke up in a dream today, to the cold of the static
And put my cold feet on the floor
…
Even though you’re so close to me, you’re still so distant
And I can’t bring you back
…
I’m with you (You, now I see, keepin’ everything inside)
With you (You, now I see, even when I close my eyes)

Another banger, very nostalgic for me, especially reminds of the DragonBallZ AMVs that used to circulate around during the good days of the Internet. If this was a part of your childhood as well, then high five!

The chorus is the core of the song, where the song says I’m with you, but I’m still keeping everything inside. You’re so distant even though you’re close to me. Maybe the worst form of isolation and detachment where you’re not able to connect with the person near you.

With You Lyrics

My December

(And I) Just wish that I didn’t feel like there was somethin’ I missed
(And I) Take back all the things I said to make you feel like that
(And I) Just wish that I didn’t feel like there was somethin’ I missed
(And I) Take back all the things that I said to you
…
And I’d give it all away
Just to have somewhere to go to
Give it all away
To have someone to come home to

The song that meets you when you’re frozen, alone and hoping for someone to share this time with. It’s a lesser known LP song, it’s very slow, no anger, no rock elements, just sadness. It’s a song about longing, maybe about past regrets, about things you want to take back, but alas you’re just there by yourself. It’s a beautiful song.

My December Lyrics

One More Light

If they say
Who cares if one more light goes out?
In the sky of a million stars
It flickers, flickers
Who cares when someone’s time runs out?
If a moment is all we are
Or quicker, quicker
Who cares if one more light goes out?
Well, I do

I end up crying a river every time I listen to this one. This song is dedicated to Chester’s memory in the music video below. But if you just listen to the words, they pierce through you like a hot knife on butter. It’s a song that gives you extreme hope and extreme sadness at the same time. For anyone who’s thought about ending it all, thinking that it doesn’t matter if just one light out of millions & billions goes out then it doesn’t make a difference, well Chester says it makes a difference to him. And it’s ironic with utmost cruelty, that Chester ended his life soon after the release of this song.

Every life is precious, and your life is connected to so many other lives in ways you probably can’t even imagine. Just think about that.

One More Light Lyrics

Wanting to change, and to be someone else

Breaking the Habit, Somewhere I Belong, Iridescent, Waiting for the End – absolute tear jerkers. You know it if you know it.

Breaking the Habit

You all assume I’m safe here in my room
Unless I try to start again
…
Clutching my cure, I tightly lock the door
I try to catch my breath again
I hurt much more than anytime before
I had no options left again
…
I don’t know how I got this way, I’ll never be alright
So I’m breaking the habit

THE song about mental health, depression and addiction. And banger of a music video as well. WATCH the video! Highly recommend.

It describes the struggle of any type of addiction perfectly. The person knows very well they have a “problem”, they want to break out of that problem / habit, they say that to themselves every single time, and every single time they fail to break through. It’s like walking through endless purgatory, trying to escape hell on one side, and reaching for heaven on the other side. But you stay .. in the middle. In the clarity of what you need to do, but in the confusion of why it doesn’t work.

Breaking the habit lyrics

Somewhere I Belong

(When this began) I had nothin’ to say
And I’d get lost in the nothingness inside of me
(I was confused) And I let it all out to find
That I’m not the only person with these things in mind
(Inside of me) But all the vacancy the words revealed
Is the only real thing that I’ve got left to feel
(Nothing to lose) Just stuck, hollow, and alone
And the fault is my own, and the fault is my own
…
I wanna heal, I wanna feel
Like I’m close to something real
I wanna find something I’ve wanted all along
Somewhere I belong

Epic rap by Mike, and epic vocals by Chester, and an overall epic song in totality. Similar to breaking the habit, this is another song where the protagonist is stuck in an inner battle, criticizing themselves for not being able to belong in a certain place or just belong in this world altogether. They KNOW they are frozen, hurt, and they long for healing, feeling and belonging. How do you escape this battle unscathed? You probably don’t, you’ll have battle scars, and you may also lose your past self, but you’ll find a way out towards somewhere you belong.

Somewhere I belong Lyrics

Iridescent

When you were standing in the wake of devastation
When you were waiting on the edge of the unknown
And with the cataclysm raining down, insides crying, “Save me now”
You were there, impossibly alone
…
Do you feel cold and lost in desperation?
You build up hope, but failure’s all you’ve known
Remember all the sadness and frustration
And let it go, let it go

A lesser known song from an incredible album from the later years of the Chester LP era. It’s a song about when you’re in that dark place, maybe during grief or a period of intense loss, or holding on to cumulative disappointments of the years, and you feel utterly lost, hopeless and alone. “And with the cataclysm raining down, insides crying, “Save me now”” — this hurts just to hear it, that a person is crying for help on the inside but still alone.

But Chester’s voice also gives you hope, a message to collect all that sadness & frustration, and throw it out the window, and just “Let it go”, and let things be how they are in that moment.

Iridescent Lyrics

Waiting for the End

Waiting for the end to come
Wishing I had strength to stand
This is not what I had planned
It’s out of my control
Flying at the speed of light
Thoughts were spinning in my head
So many things were left unsaid
It’s hard to let you go
…
(Oh-oh-oh) I know what it takes to move on
(Oh-oh-oh) I know how it feels to lie
(Oh) All I wanna do is trade this life for something new
(Oh) Holding on to what I haven’t got

The darkest song of them all, and the hardest for me to listen to, makes me choke up and cry every single damn time. This one meets you when you’re in the seventh circle, in the depths of that infernal ocean, knocking on Lucifer’s door, waiting for the dark prince to open the gates and take you in. The line that hits me extremely hard – “All I wanna do is trade this life for something new”. If you try to really feel what the song is conveying, I don’t think it’s possible to come out on the other side without having a part of you melt up.

I recommend watching this recent live performance of the song by the new LP, with Emily Armstrong as the lead singer. I absolutely love her as the new lead after Chester. No comparisons. She is just really good and has the LP soul in her, and gives the band a brand new look. I hope I can attend a live concert some day! But in this video, you can see how Emily is also crying and choking up singing this song, I’ve seen it in many videos now. She probably has something to mourn for internally or externally while singing this one.

Waiting for the End Lyrics

I guess that’s why Linkin Park still means so much to me after all these years. At 17, I loved the screaming, the heavy riffs, Mike’s rap, Chester’s voice, all the rage. At 37, I hear a completely different band. I hear the pain, loneliness, regret, hope, all the stuff I probably didn’t really understand back then, because I hadn’t experienced it myself.

The songs are still the same. I’m not.

Thanks for reading folks!

title: Book Review: Lolita by Vladimir Nabokov
excerpt: This is by far the most different book I’ve ever read. In this case, I listened to it as an audiobook. And I did it in around 5 days only, not because this was like Harry Potter that enchanted my inner child. To the contrary, listening to this book was so uncomfortable that I just […]
content:
This is by far the most different book I’ve ever read. In this case, I listened to it as an audiobook. And I did it in around 5 days only, not because this was like Harry Potter that enchanted my inner child. To the contrary, listening to this book was so uncomfortable that I just wanted to get through it as quickly as possible.

Goodreads Link

Why I chose to read this book

Bit of a backstory about why I chose to read this book. I’m in a phase of my life where I’m deliberately trying to put myself through different and uncomfortable situations so I can shake up the years of conformity, prejudices, biases and learned assumptions. I went to my Goodreads “want to read” shelf where I sadly have 190 books waiting to be read, compared to just 61 that I have actually read. Most of my list is a ton of self-help garbage that I need to purge, and then a lot of classical literature, philosophy or fantasy / science fiction. What I realized was that most of these books have no “balls” so to say, in terms of really shaking up my worldview and bringing me closer to reality instead of away from it (which the self-help and outdated classics do wonderfully). I am a big fan of Russian classic literature and probably the only time when a book has really “hit me deep” is when it came from the pen of Dostoevsky or Tolstoy or Bulgakov. So I went in search of what else do the Russian authors have in there similar to that, and that’s when I stumbled upon Lolita. I remember I had heard about this book in the past, that it was about the abhorrent subject of pedophilia and it had been banned in many countries when it came out in the 1950s. That’s when I made the choice.

The Plot

Just going to copy and paste from Wikipedia to save some time.

The protagonist and narrator is a French literature professor who moves to New England and writes under the pseudonym Humbert Humbert. He details his obsession with and victimization of a 12-year-old girl, Dolores Haze, whom he describes as a “nymphet”. Humbert becomes sexually obsessed with Dolores after becoming her stepfather, and romanticizes his obsession. Privately, he calls her “Lolita”, the Spanish diminutive for Dolores.

My takeaways

I’m going to reiterate that it’s an uncomfortable and disturbing read. Nabokov’s prose is incredible and probably the best I’ve ever read. But I think that’s one of the core takeaways as well that the prose can be beautiful while it describes an appalling reality. Also makes me think of how you can never ever assume what’s beneath the mask people put on in their daily lives. You just can’t tell who’s the predator, who’s the prey and who is suffering.

Humbert is the narrator of the book. We’re inside the monster’s mind. He describes what he does, why he does it and the meaning he assigns to facts. This is the unique thing about the book, and the tension the reader has to battle throughout. So often, as I’m listening to this while driving or while walking, I’m just exclaiming “oh my god” or “god damn” from the sheer shock of how Humbert tells you a fact about what he does to Dolores and then turns that into a romanticized story from a greek epic.

So here are my main takeaways from this wild novel:

  • Language can distort reality inside and outside — Humbert is incredibly eloquent and poetic. He continuously tries to make what he did sound romantic and aesthetically pleasing. But it’s clear that he was lying, to the reader and maybe to himself as well. Also makes me think of when I look out into the world today to find that those billionaires and politicians who have all the power come from the same mold. Beautiful language doesn’t necessarily lead to beautiful actions. I stand by that.
  • Self-awareness doesn’t necessarily lead to accountability — Humbert is remarkably self-aware and knows all about the crimes he commits, especially since he has a single-minded focus in being able to plan it all over long periods of time. He knows that he is robbing Dolores of a childhood, that he has “broken something in her”, but he does nothing to change any of it and stays centered around his desires and his own suffering.
  • Love can’t exist unless the other person is allowed to exist independently as well — it’s the classic folly of obsession veiled as love or romance. That’s what Humbert thinks and tries to convince the readers of, that he “loves” Dolores, yet his definition is only centered around his desires and wants, while at the same time he does everything in his power to control, trap and suppress Dolores from having her own identity even after taking advantage of her the whole time.

Finally, I have to say that Dolores’ story is truly tragic and you have to dig deep beneath Humbert’s poetry to find it. She doesn’t have much dialog in the book, but Humbert occasionally drops facts about her crying, feeling trapped, wanting a normal childhood, wanting to escape etc. And even in the end, she couldn’t find her freedom. It’s sad as anything could ever be, but Humbert doesn’t even let you feel that sadness. For most of the listen, I just wanted to punch the guy. It’s true.

Would I recommend reading this book?

This is not for everyone. For the longest time, I thought it wasn’t for me either, because I had this ego that I was either above or too far away from all these types of topics that have to deal with the deepest and darkest realities of the human experience, and especially for women. On the surface, I’m well aware of the horrors that young girls have to face growing up, especially in developing countries or backwards societies. It’s also one of the reasons why I sponsor 3 girls through Children.org (something I highly recommend). But I never had the courage to truly peek beneath the surface and see the horrors and the monsters. Fortunately, I’ve had people come into my life recently that have inspired me to stop staying at the surface altogether.

So, yes I would recommend reading this book if you are in an open state of mind. This novel was ahead of its time. Unfortunately, pedophilia is still a massive problem, probably larger than ever, affecting children across the world, lots of predators out there, from the poor to the powerful, who probably like Humbert romanticize their crimes while they strip away the innocence of children. Fuck them!

That’s all folks. Have a good night!

title: New art medium unlocked: Oil Pastels
excerpt: My last two posts were on art, so I’m going to continue this topic since I’m in a good flow right now, and want to see how far I can stretch my abilities with the little time I get after work. Recently, I complained about how Watercolor is hard, and then rejoiced in the comfort […]
content:
My last two posts were on art, so I’m going to continue this topic since I’m in a good flow right now, and want to see how far I can stretch my abilities with the little time I get after work.

Recently, I complained about how Watercolor is hard, and then rejoiced in the comfort of how Sketching is easy. Both of these were obviously written from my own perspective and experience with these art media over the course of my life. I had used acrylic as well in the past, but was never a fond of those paints because of how much you always had to use. Always seemed too wasteful. Watercolor is very efficient but too wild and dynamic. I don’t think I perform well under the time pressure of watercolor (similar to other things in life as well). Sketching however comes naturally to me and probably is closest to my personality as well. Simple, calm and infinitely adjustable as you can always erase what you don’t like and shade what you want to emphasize.

And all I can comment on is what I’ve tried myself. But after 37 years of life on this planet, I somehow feel like experimenting and trying out new things. Of all the paint media, I always wanted to try out oil painting for the primary reason of how good the oil paintings look. The colors, the impressionism and so much style is infused in those oil paintings, especially the classics. But, oil paints are very messy and require a well organized setup. I do not have the space or the time to delve into that right now. So, while searching on YouTube about “easier oil painting”, I stumbled upon Oil Pastels.

First, I thought we’re talking about crayons, like from kindergarten. It’s the same thing, but instead of being made just of wax, they’re made with wax and oil. Kinda like a solidified version of oil paints in my understanding. The history is interesting as well. You can read on wikipedia about how Pablo Picasso was the one who initiated the manufacturing of Oil Pastels through Sennelier. I didn’t however buy the $120 Sennelier box since I’m just starting out, so I bought the $20 Mungyo box which turned out to be more than satisfactory after my first attempt tonight.

Here is the finished artifiact:

Not bad for a first attempt I think. It absolutely exceeded my expectations on how easy it was to work with the colors here. I did follow a YouTube tutorial, so I won’t pretend to say that I could produce something like this on my own right now. But the layering approach is very intuitive, blending with fingers is straightforward although I need to get better at it, and even adding details was super easy too. No brushes or water needed. I could take my time and just add on colors when needed.

Safe to assume that I will stick with Oil Pastels for a while now and see what else comes along whenever I decide to take out this pastel paper pad, the set of colors and maybe a YT tutorial to follow-along.

Usually I engage in art whenever I’m in either a very good mood or a very pensive mood, and it always helps.

Good night folks!

title: Watercolor is hard
excerpt: I’ve had a love-hate relationship with watercolor when it comes to painting. I’ve been painting since I was a kid, and it’s always been my primary choice of paint. content:
I’ve had a love-hate relationship with watercolor when it comes to painting. I’ve been painting since I was a kid, and it’s always been my primary choice of paint. However, it’s always given me mixed results. The unpredictability of the paint and the water is what makes it hard, and unless you’ve put in the hours practicing and mastering all the techniques, you’ll always struggle. I certainly haven’t put in those hours, but I dabble nonetheless.

Saying watercolor is hard 100% of the time is probably not correct either. What probably gives people (and myself) the most pain is the wet-on-wet method, where you run a wet brush across your paper before you start painting, and then the entire painting happens while the paper continues to be wet. This method specifically is a nightmare for me because I haven’t yet understood how much I should wet the paper and how quickly I have to move through the painting to keep the effect going.

The effects in wet-on-wet are too wild and uncontrollable. Like this one below, where my perfectly fine ink sketch was destroyed by a flood of wet-on-wet effect that leaked outside the flower. Although I loved the effect itself, I couldn’t contain it.

And furthermore, the dreaded CAULIFLOWER effect, which I’ve now learned happens when there is too much water, occurs to me a lot, unfortunately! It truly feels like a chemical or oil spill, or something happening on your paper. I hate when this happens.

And when I try to be too conservative with the wetness of the paper, the strokes turn out too dry. This would have been fine if I had intended to paint in a wet-on-dry or dry-on-dry method. However, as you can see below, those clouds don’t look like clouds at all. They just look like brush strokes, which defeats the purpose of painting.

At least I like the bottom third of this sunset that I attempted to paint tonight.

Anyways. This wasn’t a venting post about how watercolor has been my friend and nemesis all my life. Maybe it was. I think it was.

In the next post, I might just share what I’m actually good at – plain old sketching. Master of the shades of grey.

Good night folks!

title: Ambivalence

content:
Lingering thoughts are afoot in the mind

Formless shapes with heavy footsteps behind

I look back and see nothing,

But I can feel the cold chaos approaching

They touch me and send a ripple through the present moment,

Taking me backward and then forward in this unforeseen torrent

I travel through time, seeing my past and future blended,

Knowing not what is true or what I have invented

I thought I knew who I was; I thought I knew where I was heading

I thought I knew what I wanted; I thought I knew what I was giving

But these are the dementors of doubt that throw me out of balance

Unsure of it all, I now beg for the golden hand of providence

There is depth in this chaos, sometimes leading to the desert, and other times to a meadow

Sounds of times past and visions of what lies beyond are all but echoes

The blood rushes to move me toward that light from the heart

Chains of fear are my only impediments to a glorious start

Pull yourself back; the world does not exist in the head

We have to live in nature, and one day sleep with the dead

Speak your mind; say what needs to be said

Stand naked on the altar of judgment instead

content:
With a thread as old as time
And my naive attempts to rhyme
I shall write a poem about hair this time

The brush that painted the Mona Lisa
The sweater that you wear
May have been a creature’s hair

A camouflage for Tigers, and the crown of Lions
Antennae for insects, and pikes for Porcupines
Nature finds a way to give meaning to these tiny vines

Galadriel’s golden strands that shine with hope
Medusa’s serpents that turn you to stone
Rapunzel’s rope, let down from her prison
In myth and prose, we find hair’s reason

From primates to humans, evolution led to attrition
Beauty for men & women, still sways our vision
Once covered in fur, we cling to a few strands
To have or how much is not in our hands

Vestigial memory of millennia from before
I know I’m a fool, I still wish I had more

title: Water

content:
Sometimes I wonder about water,

You beg for it when it’s hotter,

It was given to us and it’s within us,

It is more than just a substance that is superfluous

Is it god, being omniscient and omnipotent?

Is it ether, the container of life magnificent?

Is the crown jewel of all elements?

So important, but yet to most so insignificant?

The many forms of water are a wonder to behold,

Let’s imagine them all and see if there’s a story to be told

In a pond, it gives life to water lilies and toads,

In an ocean, the whales travel it’s mythical roads,

In a glacier, it holds the source of life,

In a river, it cuts through land like a knife,

In rain, it nourishes the trees and flowers,

In snow, it reminds me of childhood and the Christmas hours,

The master said water can flow or it crash,

It can become a bottle or a teapot in a flash,

When still, it’s a mirror that shows us our face,

When raging, it is death, and puts us in our place,

Water is creation and destruction, water is the way of living,

Still, malleable, inevitable, but ever giving,

If you follow closely, then it will always teach you lessons,

I know it now, it’s the blood of the earth and tears of the heavens

title: The Magic of Disney & Universal
excerpt: Okay so this post is a basic chronicle of my trip with two of my best friends to Disneyland & Universal in LA. This is 6 months too late, but here it is nonetheless. I’m well into my 30s now and this might seem odd to the ‘normal’ person, but these two days in LA […]
content:
Okay so this post is a basic chronicle of my trip with two of my best friends to Disneyland & Universal in LA. This is 6 months too late, but here it is nonetheless. I’m well into my 30s now and this might seem odd to the ‘normal’ person, but these two days in LA were some of the most joyous days in my life. I know it’s all capitalism, I know it’s all marketing and I had to pay a lot of money for it, but I enjoyed it. Hope you find this chronicle fun as well.

Here is my journey with a collection of some video snippets and photos. I won’t spoil it all for you in case you plan to visit in the future. And this is not sponsored by Disney or Universal. And this is just tourist-level video/photography, so please don’t bother with plagiarism. People most way more on Instagram, so I hope my post doesn’t cross any boundaries.

Day 1: Disneyland

I have to begin by expressing my deepest gratitude to my friends, who are Disney EXPERTS and planned the whole trip to perfection. They knew the strategy to maximize our chances to get on as many rides & experiences as possible, with minimal wait and still being able to enjoy every moment without anything feeling rushed. And it’s exactly how it was. We did several of the best rides multiple times (Pirates of the Caribbean), enjoyed meals together and enjoyed every moment. Bravo my dears!!

Day 1 was all Disneyland. I think we started with the Tim Burton house ride, whose name I forget, but that was my very first ride ever at Disneyland. It was amazing and laid a solid foundation for everything else to come after that. The place was packed with people of all ages, kids, parents, teenagers etc. and just had that magical vibe that they want to advertise. It was working!

After spending time in the Star Wars land, doing a couple of minor rides, we spent around an hour and a half waiting for Rise of the Resistance – apparently one of the newest and best rides at Disney. It had a LONG build-up even after we had made it to the front, with cast members dressed up as storm troopers and what not. But the ride was worth it and was a lot of fun. In the evening we made it to the more ‘classic’ side of Disney rides, starting with the Incredibles Incredicoaster.

Then the longest wait of the day was for CARS. I honestly kept wondering what could be so special about this and why there were so many people waiting for 2 hours for this ride. But man was this FUN! A whole damn race at high speed. We ended up doing this again later through the single-rider line that only had a 10 min wait. I still get thrills thinking about this one.

Even though I loved the rides, the ones that stuck with me the most, were the childhood magic rides – the little mermaid, it’s a small world and Pirates of the Caribbean (which we did 3 times I think). I was instantly transported into my childhood, with memories of watching the little mermaid cartoon in 3rd grade, getting only an hour a day to watch the TV shared with 6 members of my family in a small apartment. I felt nostalgic, grateful, happy and sad all at the same time. And still do, every time I remember these rides. #Grateful

Finally to end the day, Disney did what it does best .. create more magic with lights and music and snow!

Honorable mention — the freaking Guardians of the Galaxy ride! I did not know what I was walking into. It was HORRIBLE and AWESOME at the same time. And I’ll do it again. I’ll leave it at that.

Day 2: Universal and Hogwarts

Okay so after 30,000 steps on Day 1, we were back at it on Day 2 at Universal Studios. There was a bunch of stuff here but Hogwarts stole my heart. I am such a Harry Potter fan that I can’t describe in words (total sucker for that marketing but not sorry). Not a fan of Nintendo and didn’t get the appeal but it was a beautiful world. Although the Super Mario ride was the most horrible 4D thing and a waste of 75 mins waiting for it.

So the main highlight of the day was visiting Hogwarts. This was my dream come true. Fun fact – I did ZERO research on Disneyland and Universal before the trip and made sure to stay away from social media regarding this topic to ensure I had 100% surprise & fun. That was a great decision! I didn’t even know they had a whole actual freaking HOGWARTS CASTLE over there. So many memories there .. hogsmeade, the olivander show (where my friend was actually the CHOSEN ONE), the meal at three broomsticks, butterbeer, the freaking castle (did I mention that already?), the harry potter ride twice and then finally the Hogwarts light show at night. Dream come true!

Oh and we also did the hollywood bus tour which was super cool as well.

And some memories are good enough with photos:

Below is my very biased ranking of the rides & experiences at Disney and Universal. I’m still so so so grateful for my friends who made all this happen in just two days. I could not have done even 10% of this, had I planned myself. We had about 45,000 steps in 2 days and were completely exhausted, but it was worth every single minute!

Disney:

Universal:

That’s it. I had to document this experience so I can have more of these in the future, with my friends and my family. I still know this is all an illusion, and we’re just feeding capitalism, but until we find a way out of the drudgery of daily life, Disney offers an escape that I am fortunate and grateful to be able to visit once in a while.

Let me know your thoughts in comments below if you’ve been there or plan to visit. My friends say that the Orlando Disneyland is the real deal, so now I’ll make sure to do ZERO research about that until I make the trip some day.

title: Jim Rohn to Ready Player One — What I’ve learned from 7 books in 2022 so far
excerpt: “The person, be it gentleman or lady, who has not pleasure in a good novel, must be intolerably stupid.” — Jane Austen I adore reading, especially books. I probably read social media short-form stuff 90% of the time and books 10% of the time, but books help me learn new things 99% of the time. That 90% […]
content:
“The person, be it gentleman or lady, who has not pleasure in a good novel, must be intolerably stupid.” — Jane Austen

I adore reading, especially books. I probably read social media short-form stuff 90% of the time and books 10% of the time, but books help me learn new things 99% of the time. That 90% from social media is mostly dopamine-inducing trash. Therefore, it should be clear that I should significantly restrict my use of short-form social media for my own mental well-being; however, we’ll cover that in a later post.

I have set a 15-book reading goal for this year on Goodreads. Compared to the 25 or 50 books a year targets I’ve made during past New Year’s resolutions and never came close to attaining those, this goal is considerably more doable. So far, 7 out of 15 is not at all awful. I’ve also been reading books in a variety of media, including physical books, Audible audiobooks, and Kindle eBooks. In general, the format doesn’t really matter to me, but there has been a shift this year towards more Audiobooks. Reading a physical book is, of course, the most satisfying experience.

Books I’ve read (or listened to) in 2022 so far:

No. 1: The Ultimate Jim Rohn Library

If I could say I discovered an author this year who will stick with me until the day I die, I’d say that’s Jim Rohn. I found him on YouTube and I was instantly connected. There was something about the way this man (charisma) was talking combined with what he was saying (content) that just struck the right chord with me. It’s one of those people that tell me ‘exactly what I needed to listen’. I wanted to listen more so I got the audiobook of his complete works and have listened to it 1.5 times now. Yup. Repeat listen within a span of 3 months.

The audiobook is a mixtape of recordings from his seminars, CDs and other talks on personal development. I listened to Jim Rohn after reading Napoleon Hill and thought it would be something similar (and outdated). But I was wrong. I think his ideas are time-tested principles of personal development without any branding (something I noticed with Napoleon Hill) and delivered with a great sense of humor. I listened to most of the audio while running and so many times I’d be laughing or raising my hand in the air thinking “Yes!! Yes!! That’s exactly what I think too!”. For content that was probably released in the 70s and 80s, I could totally relate. This is probably going to be THE best collection of self-development knowledge I’ve encountered over the years and something I will repeatedly go back to whenever I need help.

No.2: Ready Player One by Ernest Cline

This book was recommended to me by my best friend when I was searching for an escape into otherworldly fiction and rightly so, she gave me one. She deserves 100% credit for all the fulfillment I received from this book. There is of course a movie by Steven Spielberg based on the novel and I had seen it before, but as my friend had pointed out — the book is nothing like the movie! It’s a totally different experience.

This audiobook was narrated by the awesome Wil Wheaton. I never knew he was THE Wesley Crusher from Star Trek — The Next Generation until I was on the 2nd chapter. That just made me happier while listening to the audiobook imagining Wesley Crusher narrating the whole thing.

The novel itself is just wonderful and I’d recommend this to any science-fiction fan. You can watch the movie too but I think the movie took out a lot of the story and focused more on the visual effects which is fine, but the story is the real gold. While going through the story, I also couldn’t help continuously compare the world created by the author to the world we might be living in soon — namely the Metaverse and it’s associated by-products like NFTs and the like. I also couldn’t help compare where this new reality might lead humanity to, a place that I don’t like at least for now. Another topic for a later post.

No. 3: Emma by Jane Austen

I mean it’s Jane Austen and this is one of her many classics. What a refreshing escape to Georgian-era England and the daily lives of men and women from that time. The Audible special was absolutely brilliant with awesome performances by the actors and accompanied by a great soundtrack (including sound effects). Many times I was surprised by sounds of horses going by while listened to the audiobook — I almost ran off the trail while running once fearing there might be a horse carriage coming behind me.

I can’t say much about the novel that hasn’t been said before about a classic of such stature. It was a delightful listen, a fulfilling story with rich characters, richer dialogue and an interesting web of love triangles that EVENTUALLY resulted in everyone getting married to the right person. Happy endings. It’s what give us people stuck in reality some hope.

No. 4: Project Hail Mary by Andy Weir

AWESOME SCIENCE-FICTION! That’s how I’d summarize this novel.

It’s written by the same author who wrote the Martian. Although I never read the book, but I did watch the movie several times, and it’s one of my favorite sci-movies ever. Project Hail Mary has a similar protagonist with the persona “I’m going to science the sh*t out of this!”. Yeah this dude did science the sh*it out of his situation as well, but it might actually be more fun, detailed and off-the-charts science-fiction that the Martian. I think they’re making a movie based on this book as well. It’ll require a ton of visual effects but if they can pull it off, could be another sci-fi classic based on a solid story.

No. 5: Magic of Thinking Big by David Schwartz

No. 6: Napoleon Hill’s Keys to Positive Thinking

No. 7: Napoleon Hill’s Golden Rules

The last three books on my completed list this year were the old-timer self-help classics. I didn’t dislike them at all, and did find the concepts quite valuable but like all good self-help books, they need to be accompanied by relatable examples. I think that’s where these books fall short, at least for me, in being relatable. I’d still refer back to the summary notes versions of these books for valuable advice.

Upcoming for the rest of 2022:

I’m not sure if I’ll be able to hit my 15 book target this year, but I’ll try my best. Following the books I’m planning to read (already started) for the balance of the year. Some of them are heavy-weights; Crime and Punishment being the heaviest by far, and some are just going to be a fun learning experience (A Mind for Numbers). I will surely post about my experiences from these books in a later post towards the end of the year.

Crime and Punishment by Fyodor Dostoevsky

Divine Comedy by Dante Alighieri

Dracula by Bram Stoker

David Copperfield by Charles Dickens

A Mind for Numbers by Barbara Oakley

If you’ve reached all the way here, then I thank you for reading this post. If you like my writing then please signup for an email subscription and follow me for more. Please comment with your thoughts as well. Thank you!

title: Return of the King

content:
“Good things come to those who wait, but only those things left by those who hustle.” – Abraham Lincoln

Sorry Mr. Tolkien for copying the title of your most magnificent third book of the LOTR series but I just had to, because I’ve always been inspired by the stories and somehow they’ve always helped me dig myself out of holes I quite often fall into.

I just realized that I started this blog somewhere in 2008 when I was 19 years old. The last time I posted was in 2016 when I was 27 and now it’s 2020 and I’m nearing the age of 31. I’ve grown mentally and physically but really I’m still the same. I’m glad that I’ve been able to maintain my core identity, principles and convictions all these years. To that point, I’ve also maintained a lot of my vices and faults – which is fine, I’m only human.

But to celebrate my return to my dear blog and my few readers, here’s a poem from the Eeshan of old.

As freedom draws you closer to fate

You start seeing the path to the gate

Through which you shall pass unseen

Like an insignificant human being

You are but stardust and one with a heart

You are but a child always at the start

Don’t move forward, Don’t move back

Just float and watch the boat in the sea

Let the current take you to your destiny

As always, most of my poetry makes sense only to me so please don’t mind. But let me know if these words evoke something in you for that is the purpose of poetry.

You’ll be seeing more of me for sure. The (still self-obsessed but not narcissistic) King has surely returned.

content:
After a long time, I finally set pen to paper or in this case, fingers to keyboard, to breathe life into my blog again. It has been 137 days since my last post Here’s one solution to Climate Change. The purpose of writing that piece was to pass an online marketing challenge given to me by a potential recruiter. Although my research and thoughts were genuine, I will not count it as a true reflection of the great introvert, which is after all the purpose of this blog. So, it has actually been 225 days since my last “reflection” New Year Reflections – Caesar, MBA and Seattle. If you have read some of my posts, then you will notice I usually start off with a quote from literature. Let’s do it again.

“Do you expect sincerity in man when hypocrisy is the very keynote of human nature? We are nurtured on it; we are schooled in it, we live by it; and we rarely realize it.”
― Rafael Sabatini, Scaramouche

It’s true. Humans are raised towards a set of rules and laws by which to live their lives. These rules and laws are not questioned, especially not when we are young and start conforming to them. And by the time we reach the age when the mind is developed and some sense of individualism can be inculcated if led towards it by an external force or just some deep inner drive, we are living in such depth of conformity that coming out of it is near impossible. Awareness of self, which is the strongest at the time of birth is lost and is replaced by unquestioned conformity. Even those who consider themselves to be “rebellious” rebel only within the socially accepted definitions of rebellion. Well, you must be wondering what is my point? There is no point in bringing this up, because what I know of being the “point” is very different from your perspective on the “point”. And maybe that is indeed the “point” of all this.

Another point of this post is to give an update to my readers about my whereabouts. I’m no longer in Cleveland, Ohio. I graduated from Case Western Reserve University‘s Weatherhead School of Management in May. Oh my! While adding a link to my school, I just noticed seeing myself in one of the videos if you scroll down to the bottom.

That is quite wonderful indeed! :)

I must mention that my 2 years at Weatherhead in Cleveland were magnificent in terms of both my educational development and my personal development. The education I received and the friends I made have left me with invaluable memories, ones that I will remember as the glorious days of my youth when I am at my end. Well now I am in Salt Lake City, Utah working for Overstock.com – a big e-retailer of primarily furniture and home decor. I work in marketing analytics, deep diving into data – finding trends, solutions and making recommendations to the business. It’s a challenging job and one that stimulates my mind. What more do I need?

That’s all I wanted to write today. I titled this post “Incoherence” but never talked about it. But the title is correct because the post itself was quite incoherent. Wasn’t it? :)

title: New Year Reflections – Caesar, MBA and Seattle
excerpt: “Cowards die many times before their deaths; The valiant never taste of death but once. Of all the wonders that I yet have heard, It seems to me most strange that men should fear; Seeing that death, a necessary end, Will come when it will come.” ― William Shakespeare, Julius Caesar A good book teaches […]
content:
“Cowards die many times before their deaths;
The valiant never taste of death but once.
Of all the wonders that I yet have heard,
It seems to me most strange that men should fear;
Seeing that death, a necessary end,
Will come when it will come.”
― William Shakespeare, Julius Caesar

A good book teaches you many things and allows you to experience truth from other people’s eyes. The truth however remains hidden until one applies that knowledge in his/her own realm of existence and discovers the validity of that truth. The above words from Julius Caesar got stuck to my thoughts when I first read the entire play a few years back and then got reinforced when I watched the 1953 movie of the same name. (If you’re interested in fiery performances, then watch the movie to experience some of the brilliance of Marlon Brando). These words say that we fear death, which is the only inevitable truth in this world. We can never be sure of anything else, but we “know” that we will die someday. Now what you do with this knowledge is open to interpretation. Some people extrapolate this and say that life is too short so just do whatever you want to do, some say that since you will die anyway then killing others is not really a sin. What is right or wrong is once again subjective and indeed subject to one’s own sense of morality. To me, this just means that I must not fear anything. I know that I do fear many a thing and most of these things are things that impede my progress towards the accomplishment of great things!

Now this is a new year post and I wanted to start it off with a type of reflection that summarizes all that I tried to do in 2015 and also gives a hint of what I will continue to do in 2016. And I think that is precisely what I did. I worked a lot on being fearless in the past year. I must say that I got a lot of opportunities to do so. The Spring semester of my MBA course was quite intense with Prof Anurag Gupta’s Risk Management course being the highlight. That one course was quite an eyeopener! I finally understand how financial systems and economies work and how budding managers like me can make a difference by effectively managing uncertainties. And after a lot of struggle I got an internship offer. I had gone through to the final round of the Google PM-intern position and didn’t make it, but after 6 rounds of interviews I did get a PM-intern offer from Amazon. I went to Seattle for 3 months and swam the seas of fire populated by fire-breathing sea-dragons! Of course I’m talking only about my job and not Seattle – which was a beautiful city during summer time.

I came back in late August to start my 3rd semester, which was one hell of a ride. Such intensity, pressure and a constant lack of time was something I experienced for the first time in my life. I daresay, that was the time I battled most of my fears and I could see myself rising to the occasion at multiple occasions. This being said, there were numerous opportunities for me to turn the “good” to “excellent” and the “excellent” to “amazing”. I’m not beating myself up or being overly self-critical (which some might see as being the purpose of this post), rather I am trying to be more aware of the things that are stopping me from being the best I can be.

I have the love of some very special people that empowers me and keeps me going. My family and a few friends. I love them and I try to be the best for them. And I know there are some people that I cannot keep happy at this moment, and that again is something I must do. I hope in time both I and they will understand. Such are the sacrifices I must make for myself for the people I love. For if I was alone in this world, I would have been content to live in the Himalayas! To these people and to everyone else, I wish a very happy new year! Make your resolutions now or whenever you feel you are ready to start something new or change something old that has been bothering you. Just like Julius Caesar says, death is certain. But everything else is uncertain. This doesn’t mean you have no control over these things. On the contrary I like to think that most of these uncertain things can be brought under control simply by working hard for whatever goal you have and for whomever you want to do whatever. There are no accidents and there are no shortcuts. There are only choices and then there is procrastination – which is not a choice, it’s just nothing.

So, onward!

content:
Prof Solow, our brilliant Statistics professor always says, “In the real world, if you’re not sure of something then AWAYS – ASK!”. He said this while explaining how to handle ambiguous demand constraints for decision modeling, but I think it is a very good life advice which can be applied to all real life situations. I’m done with his course now but I’m pretty sure that what ever he has taught us is going to stick for a long time to come.

But, I only wish that I had heard and imbibed this advice at least a couple of months before he said the words. It could have prevented me from making such weird travel plans for my home journey.

Oh! And by the way, I’m back home now! I’m in my dilli walo ki, aur meherbano ki, aur kadardaano ki, apni, saddi, pyari, dulari DILLI! I’m so happy to be with my lovely Mom, Dad and the devil brat younger brother.

Coming back to the weird travel plans, I just want to express how frantic the journey was and how less frantic it could have been if I had just asked somebody before booking the tickets. I “assumed” that since I booked through Lufthansa, I will be allowed 2 checked bags, but the polite United Airlines folks politely charged me a hundred dollars for the extra bag despite my theatrical efforts to dissuade them from doing so. I traveled to 4 different airports – Cleveland, New Jersey, New York, Frankfurt and Delhi. Oh, that’s five! New Jersey to New York was a shared shuttle ride in bad rush hour traffic. All the flights very were delayed for the same reason – someone got sick just before the flight and had to get off, along with the baggage. Finding the baggage among the thousands caused the most delay. This was seriously weird. I was even thinking about Final Destination at some point; the person who had a vision of the plane exploding got off and later on the plane did explode and all that weird stuff. Moreover, the layovers were very tight. At Frankfurt, I had to literally run from gate Z to gate C (train ride included) to catch the last flight. And to top it all, my stomach troubled me throughout the flight and I did not get an ounce of sleep even though I tried everything (including listening to nature sounds while the person on my left was snoring like a pig – that was also a nature sound but not to my liking!).

I did not sleep for 35 hours straight and covered 8,094 miles in 27 hours. What an invention! Airplanes! I would however want to try such journeys by ship someday, when I’m free from the constraints of time. But now I’m back and I’m going to forget all of this and enjoy mom’s world best awesomest food, and will go and see places and meet friends and celebrate the new year!

At least until my return journey which is exactly the same as this one.

title: Natalie MacMaster at the Cleveland Orchestra
excerpt: I have always had a penchant for classical music (besides my crazy love for scream-o metal music). The symphonies of Beethoven and the violin concertos of Vivaldi have been my “soul” music for many years now. Whether to study or to just calm the mind, I listen to them time and again – a small proof […]
content:
I have always had a penchant for classical music (besides my crazy love for scream-o metal music). The symphonies of Beethoven and the violin concertos of Vivaldi have been my “soul” music for many years now. Whether to study or to just calm the mind, I listen to them time and again – a small proof of the timelessness of such epic music. I had always wondered how such deeply moving music is made, who makes it and how does the sound come out so perfectly. I knew there were orchestras and closest to those I had seen were in the Tom and Jerry cartoons.

But when I came to Cleveland, I found out that there was an orchestra which used to play at a place barely 3 blocks away from my college. Now that was convenient! And as is the case with every new thing that comes my way, I had to go see it. I attended the performance of Beethoven’s 6th Symphony – “Pastoral” conducted by world-famous Franz Welser-Möst and performed mostly by Professors here at the famous Cleveland Institute of Music. What an experience! That was when space-time warped around me and I was shot through a wormhole into the other side of the galaxy, all the way experiencing the sights and sounds of an idyllic paradise. It got me hooked on the Cleveland Orchestra.

Tonight was my 8th concert of the season since I started attending in mid-September. Not to take anything away from the previous ones, tonight was the most fun concert of them all. I will not forget this one for a long time to come.

Natalie MacMaster from Nova Scotia, Canada. World-famous fiddler, mother of 6 children, brilliant orator, superb stage performer and truly inspirational personality. She played Celtic and Folk music on her fiddle (an instrument very much akin to the violin but having a different sound – you gotta hear it to know it). The program lasted for 2 hours plus a 15 minute intermission and for every single moment of the show, I and supposedly the whole audience was on edge, the edge of pure happiness and fun.

The program started off with a lively prelude by the orchestra, a symphony more akin to some Hobbit or Lord of the Rings style epic background score. Then came in Natalie MacMaster, with Mac Morin on the grand piano and Eric Breton on percussion. I must also mention that Severance Hall for lighted up for Christmastime and her entry also brought in a change in lights; the whole concert hall glowing purple and pink – a treat for the eyes! She started off with such an energy and a body language that everyone in the audience was resonating with her in some way or the other. A couple of elderly ladies were really enjoying the music. And to top that, she was tap dancing while playing! In the second melody, Mac Morin left his piano and performed a splendid tap dance. She was vibrating with energy, dancing and playing at the same, moving from one part of the stage to another, the audience clapping along with the beats of her heels!

In the second part of the program, she also played one of her sober compositions – “If ever you were mine” – she recorded this one first when she was 19 yrs old in 1991. Here is a YouTube link for those who would be interested. Between melodies, she took up the mine and talked to the audience, telling some or the other funny story about her family or herself. I really admired her love for her family, especially for a person so dedicated to their craft, their work and one who has near the pinnacle of her career. The program ended with a not so surprising standing ovation, which lasted for around 10 minutes, the audience clapping and getting a bonus performance as well! My hands were hurting after the clapping stopped but it was all for someone who deserved it. This performance could easily sway the crowds of a rock music festival. As for me, I became a life-long fan of Ms MacMaster!

While searching YouTube for some more performances by her, I came across one where she performing on stage with her little kids! A must-watch! Enjoy!

title: Eeshan’s MBA Course: 25% Completed
excerpt: It takes an extremely intense educational program coupled with a new life requiring self-sustainability, responsibility and no less degree of adventure to stop me from writing for my blog for such a long time. I ventured into this new life in a new land full of new people 4 months ago, when I set foot […]
content:
It takes an extremely intense educational program coupled with a new life requiring self-sustainability, responsibility and no less degree of adventure to stop me from writing for my blog for such a long time. I ventured into this new life in a new land full of new people 4 months ago, when I set foot in Cleveland, a historic city in Ohio state of the United States of America. My objective was to obtain an MBA degree from the renowned Weatherhead School of Management at Case Western Reserve University. I had heard from people that an MBA course is intense, hectic, crazy, stupid and many more random adjectives describing it. I used to respond with a simple “meh”. That was 4 months ago.

4 months have passed, today was the last day of the first semester, culminating with the end of the final exams, this one being on Economics. I now say “daaaaammmmmmnnnnn!!!”.

Finally, I get a break! This was crazy intense! One semester, 5 subjects, 2 part-time jobs, constant internship search, living on my own for the first time in my life, cleveland orchestra, chipotle, pizza and the extreme extreme extreme cold! Welcome to the first part of my adventure.

I’m so glad that it’s over. I am proud to have been through it and come out unscathed without a nervous breakdown and maybe much tougher than before. What an experience! The kind of people I met here, I may never have got a chance to meet if I had not come here. My classmates, each and every one of them is a story, rather an institution in themselves. I have learned so much, yet I think I have only scratched the surface of what is seemingly an endless source of knowledge and experience for me. I have yet to open the jammed doors of my emotional fortress to all these people who are a constant and rich outflow of energy and passion. It is a people-centric culture here, unlike the task-centric culture to which I had adjusted so well during my 3 1/2 years on the job doing hardcore software engineering. I am training to be a manager, a leader and a good person, so I expect myself to make some changes which I am sure will come around sooner or later.

Today I am 25% closer to my goal and realize that I have 25% less time to do what I have to do. Whilst I understand that time pressure always ruins heartfelt dreams, but hopefully it will help me prioritize and manage my daily activities towards the right direction.

I miss my home and my parents and my brother everyday. It makes me sad everyday not being there with them. I miss my friends too. There is still a great deal of chaos in my mind, a turbulence that does not settle down. That’s the whole point of an adventure I guess. I know not what’s in store for me. But I know that fortune favors the brave and I must be brave … like Aragorn! ;)

content:
Poem No.2 for my daily gratitude ritual on Happier! https://www.happier.com/

Give some water, earth and light to a tiny seed

then behold a wonder that results from this deed

the seed erupts, crawls up to the sky with skinny shoots

and sinks deep into the soil with tiny roots

father time nurtures the seed and its tiny extensions

and it grows and grows without any pretensions

the first leaf is a sign of coming green

and a flag marking victory of forces unseen

branch to branch with leaves asunder

hold your breath for the next wonder

the seed becomes a tree when a branch bears the first fruit

and slowly but surely every other follows suit

the canopy expands, the fruits multiply

small creatures begin to arrive from the sky

some arrive from beneath in search of a home

they build their nests and they build their domes

the tree bears all, benevolent and great

every creature now bound to its fate

it gives shelter to the wet and shade to hot

such grandeur came from a tiny seed, forget that not!

Well, this post is not really about grammar, it’s about a great book I read known as “The Lord of the Rings“. Before I delve into a critical account, I would just let my inner child say … “this was the most fantastically fantasical super awesome oh god in hell superb Aragorn! Gandalf! Go to hell Sauron! I loved it!!”

Whuff! Now that its out, I can be more sober. ;)

This work was written a long time ago and one can argue that the World Wars in Tolkien’s may have influenced his work, but I do not believe so as The Lord of the Rings is only an account of a brief period of the Third Age. Tolkien, a linguist by profession, created his own world, complete with detailed history, geography, mythology, sociology and everything else. A parallel universe as wondrous as the real, if not more. Personally I would liked to have been born in his universe rather than my present one, but you know the saying, “the grass looks greener on the other side”.

The Lord of the Rings consists of three books:

  1. The Fellowship of the Ring
  2. The Two Towers
  3. The Return of the King

After reading this large volume, I can now say something about Tolkien’s style of writing. He paid great attention to detail. The geography of every land encountered by Frodo or Gandalf‘s company was described beautifully, and in words only known to an expert in this field. It might be too much for a reader to grasp initially but if you just try to guess the meanings and go along, you eventually reach a stage when the scenery just starts to display right in front of your eyes. It is the most amazing geographical detail style I have ever read in any book. Similarly, every character was described in detail, from his/her appearance to personality. And everything had a history associated with it, whether land or human, a clear reference only possible by reading his complete works, but wondrous nonetheless.

For me, this book (and the movies) are very close to what I seek in knowledge. There are so many life lessons I took away from it, such as, the importance of simple things, the growing, dying and passing away of man, lands and everything, the concept of time, which played a major role here. And the tales of heroism, of war, of the plots of evil, and the persistence of a man’s heart, had so much to teach me.

I would recommend any serious reader to relish this beautiful stream of words and bask in the glory of its suchness. I will read it again and again for I am sure I will find something new every time.
